hints: Since the degrees of the numerator and denominator are both 2, divide first to find the constant quotient.
Factor the quadratic denominator $2x^2 - 5x - 12$ into linear factors $(2x + 3)(x - 4)$.
Express the remaining proper algebraic fraction in partial fractions $\dfrac{A}{2x + 3} + \dfrac{B}{x - 4}$.
walkthrough:
Factor the denominator $2x^2 - 5x - 12$:
Find factors of $2(-12) = -24$ that add to $-5$: these are $-8$ and $+3$.
$$2x^2 - 8x + 3x - 12 = 2x(x - 4) + 3(x - 4) = (2x + 3)(x - 4)$$

Divide the numerator by the denominator to obtain the polynomial quotient:
$$\dfrac{6x^2 - 9x - 16}{2x^2 - 5x - 12} = 3 + \dfrac{(6x^2 - 9x - 16) - 3(2x^2 - 5x - 12)}{2x^2 - 5x - 12}$$

Set up partial fractions for the proper remainder fraction:
$$\dfrac{6x + 20}{(2x + 3)(x - 4)} = \dfrac{A}{2x + 3} + \dfrac{B}{x - 4}$$
Multiply through by $(2x + 3)(x - 4)$:
$$6x + 20 = A(x - 4) + B(2x + 3)$$

Determine constant $A$ by setting $x = -\dfrac{3}{2}$:
$$6\left(-\dfrac{3}{2}\right) + 20 = A\left(-\dfrac{3}{2} - 4\right) + B(0)$$
$$-9 + 20 = A\left(-\dfrac{11}{2}\right)$$
$$11 = -\dfrac{11}{2}A \implies A = 11 \times \left(-\dfrac{2}{11}\right) = -2$$

Combine the quotient and partial fractions into the final expression:
$$3 - \dfrac{2}{2x + 3} + \dfrac{4}{x - 4}$$
